To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a method to represent disordered nanoporous materials, and we have used this to study thin films with a range of pore sizes and porosities.
we have developed a method of representing the morphology of nanoporous thin films, and that the morphology is disorted, with the pores being interconnected, at a porosity as low as 10%.

the pore morphology can be described by a fractal dimension that is a function of the porosity, the pore size scale is on the order of the pore separation (pore separation/pore size ~ 1.5), the pores are interconnected for porosities greater than 10%, and the pore morphology changes from a sponge-like morphology to a more open morphology as the porosity is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of methods for the determination of pore morphologies in disorted nanoporous thin films, and the application of this information for the design of materials with desired properties.
understanding the relationship between the structure and the properties of nanoporous thin films, with the goal of being able to tailor the properties of the film by controlling the structure.
the characterization of the structure of nanoporous thin films, and we have developed a method of generating three-dimensional representations of pore morphologies from small-angle scattering data.

the pore morphology is disordered with the pores being interconnected at a length scale of 20 nm.

we have shown that small-angle X-ray data from disordered porous materials can be used to generate representative three-dimensional morphological structures, which in turn can be used to determine pore size, extent of interconnection and connectivity of pore space.
the method described here provides a powerful tool for determining the morphology of a wide range of materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for generating representative 3D morphologies for a range of disordered nanoporous materials, which is applicable to any porous material, regardless of its chemical composition or pore size.

we can use X-ray scattering to generate representative three-dimensional models of nanoporous thin films with disordered morphologies, and that we can use these models to determine the pore size scale, interconnection, and transitions between closed, interconnected, and bicontinuous pore morphologies.
we have developed a method for characterizing the morphologies of disordered nanoporous materials and have used this to characterize the morphologies of nanoporous thin films.

the morphology of the pore structure can be characterized in a way that is not possible using traditional characterization methods such as SEM or TEM.
we have developed a method of representing a complex pore morphology that allows us to determine the pore connectivity as well as the pore size scale.

the pore morphologies of nanoporous materials can be described by simple models that are useful for understanding the relationship between pore size scale and connectivity and for interpreting scattering data.
